::: {.atlas-intro}
# fMRI models, from events to inference

fmrimod is a Python library for hemodynamic response functions, experimental
designs, first-level GLMs, contrasts, and group analysis. Describe the model,
fit it to preprocessed data, and inspect the results at each step.

::: {.reading-links}
[Install and fit a model](get-started.qmd)
[Browse the tutorials](tutorials/index.qmd)
[Explore the figure gallery](tutorials/plot-gallery.qmd)
[Look up an API](reference/index.qmd)
:::
:::

## A contrast in brain space

Two runs of the published FIAC experiment, one participant, and a
same-sentence minus different-sentence contrast. Image geometry stays with
the estimates through the fit and back to a brain map.

These are uncorrected t statistics after 6 mm smoothing of the BOLD data.
The tutorial explains the design, pooling choice, and comparison receipt.

[Work through the FIAC analysis](tutorials/real-data-fiac.qmd)
:::
:::

::: {.atlas-body}
## See what goes into the model

Event timing becomes a regressor only after choosing a hemodynamic response
function (HRF). Compare the response shapes, inspect the design columns,
and check what a contrast asks of those columns before interpreting a map.

::: {#ed6c2b8e .cell fig-height='3.2' fig-width='9' execution_count=2}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![Two HRF choices, each normalized to unit peak for this comparison. Equal peaks here do not imply equal native amplitude conventions.](index_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=780 height=352 fig-alt='SPM canonical and gamma hemodynamic response curves normalized to unit peak, showing different response shapes.'}
:::
:::


The [figure gallery](tutorials/plot-gallery.qmd) shows the current model,
fit, and residual inspection plots. [Explore the plotting guide](tutorials/plotting-visualization.qmd) or
[estimate an HRF from data](tutorials/estimating-hrfs.qmd), with fitted curves
and uncertainty intervals.

## Follow an analysis

::: {.analysis-route}
### [Events and design](tutorials/design-matrices.qmd)

Write an event table, select an HRF, and inspect the regressors and their
correlations. Add baseline terms and parametric modulators as needed.
:::

::: {.analysis-route}
### [Fit and contrast](tutorials/linear-model.qmd)

Fit a first-level GLM and compare named conditions. Follow a simulated effect
through the [complete workflow](tutorials/golden-path.qmd), or estimate
[responses to individual trials](tutorials/single-trial.qmd).
:::

::: {.analysis-route}
### [Group and diagnostics](tutorials/group-analysis.qmd)

Collect subject contrasts, choose a group model, and examine its results.
[Group diagnostics](tutorials/group-diagnostics.qmd) distinguish unusual
subject maps from subjects that strongly influence the pooled estimate.
:::

::: {.status-note}
fmrimod is source-installable alpha software for Python 3.10 and newer.
The [evidence guide](evidence/index.qmd) explains the checked-in comparisons
with R, Nilearn, and FitLins, including the
[active numerical caveats](https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/fmrimod/blob/main/docs/contracts/CAVEATS.md).
:::
:::
